title: Visual Branch is What You Need for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.37888v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) requires models to recognize new classes over time without forgetting previously learned ones. With the rise of vision-language pre-training, CLIP has become a strong foundation for CIL. A common design in CLIP-based CIL is to construct textual classifier weights by encoding class-name templates with the CLIP text encoder, and then classify visual features by image-text cosine similarity. This design is appealing: since CLIP aligns images and text in a shared embedding space, textual weights appear to provide an off-the-shelf classifier for incremental classes. However, we show that this seemingly natural design is not always beneficial, as a modality gap can still separate the two modalities and make textual classifier weights deviate from visual class distributions. translated_title: 视觉分支就是基于CLIP的类增量学习所需要的一切
translated_abstract: 类增量学习要求模型在不断识别新类别的同时不遗忘之前学到的类别。随着视觉-语言预训练的兴起，CLIP已成为类增量学习的强大基础。基于CLIP的类增量学习中的一个常见设计是：使用CLIP文本编码器对类别名称模板进行编码，构建文本分类器权重，然后通过图像-文本余弦相似度对视觉特征进行分类。这种设计很有吸引力：由于CLIP在共享嵌入空间中对齐了图像和文本，文本权重似乎可以为增量类别提供现成的分类器。然而，我们表明这种看似自然的设计并非总是有益的，因为模态差距仍然可能将两种模态分隔开，使文本分类器权重偏离视觉类别的分布。实验表明，在相同的任务级类增量学习训练下，用视觉类中心初始化余弦分类器可以获得更低的损失和更好的性能。
tldr: 该论文揭示了基于CLIP的类增量学习中因模态差距导致文本分类器权重偏离视觉类别分布，提出直接用视觉类中心初始化余弦分类器即可取得更低损失和更好性能，证明视觉分支才是关键。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that the modality gap makes textual classifier weights deviate from visual class distributions in CLIP-based class-incremental learning, and simply initializing the cosine classifier with visual class centers yields lower loss and better performance, proving that the visual branch is what you need.
